name: Muodo
body:
In their pursuit of creating larval trox, the Atlanteans went through several periods of trial and error. One collection of variations they discarded were the muodo.

Muodos are variant trox, left to survive or die on shattered worlds the Atlanteans believed couldn’t be saved. What their progenitors didn’t account for was the muodos’ will to live. Because of their already manipulated genetics, the creatures quickly evolved and adapted, creating societies of their own and succeeding where the Atlanteans gave up. The next time a Mejn? Shift brought the reality-hopping culture back, the muodos were ready to show why they were worth more than how they were treated.

Physical Description: All muodos have traces of trox genes in their own, making them large, giving them multiple limbs, or covering them in a strong outer shell. The statistics here represent the most common of muodo, with smaller heritages standing half as tall and weighing one-quarter as much on average.

Society: Muodo society has taken necessary evolution to the extreme, adapting to environments uninhabitable to most due to extreme magic, radiation, or other toxic and deadly effects. By using the added intelligence given them by the Atlanteans to curb their animal instincts, the muodo have formed a society where not only the strong rule, and the inventive can reign under the right circumstances.

Base Height	Base Weight	Weight Modifier	Modifier
8 ft. 9 in.	320 lbs.	3d12	x16
Adult	Middle Age	Old	Venerable	Maximum Age
4	18	32	46	+3d10 years

Relations: Muodos get along well with non-Atlanteans, and the odd muodo is even willing to work with their creators at least in temporary situations, but an innate sense of self protection keeps any muodo from every truly trusting that an Atlantean wouldn’t put them at risk given the chance.

Alignment & Religion: Muodos are chaotic, but not due to any fault of their own. Their spliced and re-spliced genetics are just naturally more in tune with the Chaos and its various minions. Muodo society never had time to develop religion of its own; it was too busy learning to make due with reality. While muodo adventurers can and do often find religion in their travels, the larger culture views such practices largely as a waste of time.

Adventurers: Studying the remnants of the Atlantean technology that stranded them, the muodo have been able to send some of their kind across realities to learn more and eventually bridge those worlds to their own.

Names: Muodos combine Atlantean and Troxian naming conventions. The result are names that sound almost human, such as Dom, Geo, Mathis, and Shashandar.

Ancestry Traits (Advanced)
Ability Score Modifiers: +4 Strength, +2 Intelligence, –2 Dexterity, –2 Charisma. Muodos are among the strongest, most evolved species on their world, but their size limits their mobility and their appearance can be terrifying to some.
Size: Large. As Large creatures, muodos take a –1 size penalty to their AC, a –1 size penalty on attack rolls, and a –4 size penalty on Stealth checks They gain a +1 bonus on combat maneuver checks and to their CMD. Muodos take up a space that is 10 feet by 10 feet and have a reach of 5 feet.
Speed: A muodo’s base speed is 30 feet.
Troxian: Like the trox, muodos are monstrous humanoids with darkvision out to 60 feet.
Multi-Armed: Muodos possess four arms. A muodo can wield multiple weapons, but only one hand is its primary hand, and all others are off hands. It can also use its hands for other purposes that require free hands.
Antimagic Shell: A muodo can cast antimagic field on itself, filling its space only. This functions as the spell, except it lasts for a duration of concentration up to 3 rounds. At 4th level and above, the duration is concentration up to 1 round/level. A muodo parasite can use this ability a number of times per day equal to its Constitution modifier (minimum 1). While antimagic shell is in effect, a muodo with the ability to cast spells can attempt a concentration check (DC 20 + twice the spell level) to cast a spell without a duration of concentration on another creature or in an area outside of its shell. If it fails at the check, the muodo loses the spell as if it had cast it to no effect.
Languages: A muodo human begins play speaking Common and Terran. Those with high Intelligence scores can choose any languages they want (except for secret languages, such as Druidic).
Muodo Parasite (Advanced)

Muodo parasites are bat-like insectoids with wings instead of extra arms. They are smaller than the average muodo, but no less dangerous in the right environment.

Muodo parasites have all the same ancestry traits as muodos, except as noted here.

Ability Score Modifiers: +2 Strength, +2 Intelligence, –2 Charisma. These ability score adjustments are standard, without the size bonuses or penalties.
Size Medium. Muodo parasites are Medium creatures. They gain no bonuses or penalties due to their size, their space is 5 feet by 5 feet, and their reach is 5 feet.
Winged. Instead of 4 arms, muodo parasites have a pair of wings they use to fly. These muodos have a fly speed of 30 feet with average maneuverability. This trait replaces multi-armed.
Favored Class Bonuses

When you gain your first favored class bonus, choose one class to which all of the below options apply.

Any: Gain 1/6 of a use of antimagic shell per day.
Any: Gain 1/3 of a use of dispel magic per day. Casting dispel magic in this way spends 1 use of antimagic shell, and the muodo uses its character level as its caster level with this ability.
Any: Gain 1/3 of a use of greater dispel magic per day. This favored class bonus can only be selected once for every use of dispel magic the muodo has and functions in the same way.
Any: Gain 1/3 of a use of antimagic field per day. This favored calss bonus can only be selected once for every use of greater dispel magic the muodo has and functions in the same way.
Muodo Class Options
Muodo Barbarian

A muodo barbarian can select any muodo ancestry feat as a barbarian rage power, but can only use those feats when raging. In addition, the muodo barbarian can use and concentrate on his antimagic shell while raging.

This alters the barbarian’s rage powers and replaces fast movement.

Muodo Fighter

Muodo fighters are not proficient with heavy armor, but they do gain a +1 natural armor bonus and the Alert combat trait at 1st level (Once per day as a free action, the muodo fighter can take 10 on its initiative check.). This natural armor bonus increases by +1 at 3rd, 7th, 11th, and 15th level. In addition, they can select muodo ancestry feats as fighter feats one level before other characters if they meet all other prerequisites of those feats.

This alters the fighter’s bonus feats and armor proficiencies, and replaces armor training.

Muodo Key Guardian

Muodo key guardians can select muodo ancestry feats in place of keybind powers. The key guardian can only benefit from those feats by spending 1 energy, but can use them more than once per day as long as it has the energy to spend. If the feat doesn’t have its own duration (such as spell resistance), it lasts for up to 1 round per key guardian level for each 1 energy spent.

Muodo Makari

At 1st, 3rd, 11th, and 19th level, a muodo makari can trade finesse training for a muodo ancestry feat, but it must have at least 1 panache point remaining to gain that feat’s benefits.

At 3rd level, a muodo makari with at least 1 panache point can concentrate to maintain its antimagic shell as a swift action. It can also spend 1 panache point when it uses antimagic shell to gain those benefits for up to 3 rounds without concentrating.

This replaces either high jump or makari initiative, and the makari can select the replaced power in place of another at later levels.

Muodo Rogue

Muodo rogues can select muodo ancestry feats in place of rogue talents one level before other characters if they meet all other prerequisites of those feats.
